documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy: how it applies to generative AI
documents.stance_why: The page says "what is permitted depends on your course" and quotes the policy that permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment"; it sets no default itself and leaves the decision to courses and assignments, so delegates.
documents.summary: Explains that Syracuse's Academic Integrity Policy leaves AI permissions to each course and assignment, and that students remain responsible for the work. Defines generative AI and says users must review and make AI content their own.

units.why: This page applies the Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. The quoted sentence says permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", so the rule is left to each course and assignment; it is a statement of fact about variation, hence P04 (not P85, which concerns schools or units).
units.anchor: may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment

units.why: This page applies the Academic Integrity Policy to generative AI. The same sentence says the variation rests "on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment", tying AI decisions to learning objectives, which is P83 and not P04 because it states the basis rather than who decides.
units.anchor: based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment

units.why: The page defines the tools it governs: "These tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases". This sets what generative AI means for the guidance, so it is a definition (P61), informs.
units.anchor: These tools generate new content

units.why: "Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation" says AI work needs a human to direct and judge it, keeping the person as the thinker (P32); a general principle so informs. P31 is not chosen because it concerns verifying correctness, which the next sentence covers.
units.anchor: Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation.

units.why: The sentence makes it "our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy", a duty to verify AI output (P31). Modality is must because "responsibility" is stated as an obligation; the "make it our own" clause is coded separately as P29.
units.anchor: revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it our own
units.policy: Users are responsible for reviewing and revising AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy.

units.why: The same sentence adds that users must "make it our own", i.e. the content they use is theirs. That is ownership of work (P29), separate from the verification duty above.
units.anchor: make it our own
units.policy: Users are responsible for making AI-generated content their own.

units.why: The page subtitle says "the responsibility for the work stays with you", directly addressing students: whatever AI is used, responsibility for the work stays with the student, which is P29.
units.anchor: the responsibility for the work stays with you

documents.unit: Center for Teaching and Learning Excellence / Academic Integrity Office
documents.title: Syllabus Requirements (required AI language statements)
documents.stance_why: The saved text is the Academic Integrity Resources page. It lists links such as "Required Syllabus Language" but contains no AI statement or AI rule itself; no stance can be read from it, so delegates is the closest label (syllabus language is left to faculty), with only one general integrity unit coded.
documents.summary: The saved page is the Academic Integrity Office resources index (advisors, FAQs, forms). It links to required syllabus language but the fetched text holds no generative-AI wording; 'AI' there abbreviates Academic Integrity.

units.why: The only student-facing duty tied to the integrity policy in this text is "provide their electronic signature agreeing to uphold the AI policy" (AI here abbreviates Academic Integrity, not artificial intelligence). It is general integrity-policy communication that would cover AI misuse but never mentions AI use; no type fits, so UNCOVERED, low confidence.
units.anchor: provide their electronic signature agreeing to uphold the AI policy
units.uncovered_note: Students must read the Academic Integrity expectations and e-sign agreement twice a year (general integrity, not specific to generative AI).

documents.title: AI for Students
documents.stance_why: The page quotes that permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment" and itself only welcomes AI ("ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI") and lists tools and data cautions; it sets no course-level rule, so delegates.
documents.summary: ITS student hub for generative AI: quotes the university integrity rule, lists university-provided AI tools and the approved list for University data, and suggests study and career uses. Overlaps the AI policy page.

units.why: The ITS student page opens with a note quoting the Academic Integrity Policy. The quoted sentence says permitted AI use "may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", so the rule is left to each course and assignment; it is a statement of fact about variation, hence P04 (not P85, which concerns schools or units).
units.anchor: may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment

units.why: The ITS student page opens with a note quoting the Academic Integrity Policy. The same sentence says the variation rests "on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment", tying AI decisions to learning objectives, which is P83 and not P04 because it states the basis rather than who decides.
units.anchor: based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment

units.why: The page repeats the definition of generative AI ("These tools generate new content based on existing data") to scope the guidance; a definition so P61, informs.
units.anchor: based on existing data from the internet or other databases

units.why: "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy" is a duty to check AI output, so P31; stated as responsibility, hence must.
units.anchor: review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it our own
units.policy: Users are responsible for reviewing and revising AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy.

units.why: "make it our own" makes the content used the user's own responsibility, which is P29 and distinct from the accuracy-checking duty (P31).
units.anchor: make it our own
units.policy: Users are responsible for making AI-generated content their own.

units.why: "ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI into your day-to-day" welcomes and promotes student AI use, so P02 with unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI into your day-to-day

units.why: "Claude Enterprise ... now available to Syracuse University faculty, staff, and students" provides a university-licensed AI tool for everyone, institution-wide rather than one course, so P92 (not P17, which is course-specific).
units.anchor: now available to Syracuse University faculty, staff, and students

units.why: "Microsoft Copilot is now powered by OpenAI's latest GPT-5 model" with login via University credentials lists another university-provided tool for all users, so P92.
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot is now powered by OpenAI’s latest GPT-5 model

units.why: "Google Gemini ... also is available" with g.syr.edu credentials is a further university-provided tool, so P92.
units.anchor: Use your netid@g.syr.edu credentials when logging in.

units.why: "Clementine is your AI guide to Syracuse University" describes a university-built AI assistant. P92 would also fit, but Clementine is built by Syracuse as a campus guide, so P17 (provide a sanctioned tool) is the nearest.
units.anchor: Clementine is your AI guide to Syracuse University.
units.fit_note: Tool is a campus-wide guide built by the university, not a course tool.

units.why: The guidelines are said to "ensure the ethical and responsible use of AI technologies by students, faculty, staff and vendors", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, P56.
units.anchor: ensure the ethical and responsible use of AI technologies

units.why: "users should only enter University data after logging in with their University credentials ... to the following tools" limits where University data goes to approved tools; this is the use-approved-tools rule (P92). P50 is used for the companion sentence about other tools.
units.anchor: users should only enter University data after logging in with their University credentials
units.policy: Users should only enter University data into the listed approved AI tools after logging in with their University credentials.
units.fit_note: Framed around University data and security standards, not a general tool-choice rule.

units.why: "University community members should not use University data when working in any other AI tools" protects University data by excluding unvetted tools, so P50 (protect data, prefer vetted tools); should-not.
units.anchor: should not use University data when working in any other AI tools

units.why: "Creating effective study schedules and routines" names an allowed study use of AI; nearest is P14 (study aids), with a fit note.
units.anchor: Creating effective study schedules and routines
units.fit_note: Study planning, not practice problems or summaries.

units.why: "Organizing group study sessions and materials" is a listed potential use of AI for studying, P14 (study aids).
units.anchor: Organizing group study sessions and materials
units.fit_note: Organizing study sessions, not generating study content.

units.why: "Brainstorming creative project ideas and themes" is a listed potential use, matching P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming creative project ideas and themes

units.why: "Preparing thoughtful questions for office hours" suggests using AI to get ready to ask a human instructor; nearest is P72 (human help alongside AI), but here AI prepares for human help.
units.anchor: Preparing thoughtful questions for office hours
units.fit_note: AI is used to prepare for human help rather than students being directed to human help.

units.why: "Preparing for job interviews and career fairs" is a listed potential AI use that is career preparation; no type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Preparing for job interviews and career fairs
units.uncovered_note: Students may use AI to prepare for job interviews and career fairs.

units.why: "Planning balanced meal prep for busy weeks" is a listed potential AI use unrelated to coursework, so no type fits: UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Planning balanced meal prep for busy weeks
units.uncovered_note: Students may use AI for personal life tasks such as meal planning.

units.why: "generative AI can offer creative solutions and fresh perspectives" names a benefit of AI for students without a rule or a career claim, so P87.
units.anchor: generative AI can offer creative solutions and fresh perspectives

units.why: "will continue to add resources to this hub as the field evolves" says the guidance will be updated as AI changes, P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: will continue to add resources to this hub as the field evolves

notes: syracuse-u2 saved text is the Academic Integrity Resources index; it contains no generative-AI rule (AI there means Academic Integrity), so only one general integrity-communication unit was coded (UNCOVERED, not AI-specific). The three-statement syllabus requirement described in the collect file is not in the saved text and was not coded.
